result:
The upper bound in Solution 3 is valid: two vertices on the same side of a $K_{t,t}$ have exactly $t$ common neighbours, so they determine that copy, and each copy covers $t(t-1)$ same-side pairs. Its construction also checks out. Adjacency $w+v=\pi((x+y)^2)$ gives exactly $t$ common neighbours for every pair with $x\neq y$, and the common neighbourhood of such a pair completes to a $K_{t,t}$. The pairs with $x=y$ number $o(n^2)$. So the copy count is $(1-o(1))\binom{n}{2}/(t(t-1))$, giving $\frac{1}{2t(t-1)}$.

Solution 1's $1/t!$ is unsupported, and Solution 2's bound fails because a family of $t$-subsets of $N(v)$ pairwise meeting in at most one vertex can have size quadratic in $\deg(v)$, not linear.

CHOICE: 3
CONFIDENCE: 4
